correctness.rationale: The unit cuts generate input increments modulo constants with l1 coefficient norm equal to input variation. On a strict order chamber each cut gives entries in {−1,0,1} supported on at most three consecutive windows. For output lengths 1,2,3,4,≥5 this bounds variation by 0,2,4,5,6 respectively. Integrating the chamber bounds gives the global estimate; a common generic perturbation of the two endpoints handles a segment lying in a tie hyperplane by continuity without changing their difference. The displayed rank-preserving perturbations attain the bounds and extending the baseline from length eight adds no straddling windows. For one input the layer-cake integral over binary exact-two windows and the discrete coarea identity reduce the estimate to the 16-state binary potential, whose 32 transition inequalities telescope against the input jumps. The length-five replacement has slopes 0,−1,1,0 between the fixed samples and gives bound 1; length four gives zero. Binary step witnesses attain the reported nonzero constants. value.rationale: A local robust spread statistic can have small ordinary output variation while substantially amplifying the variation of differences of nearby inputs. The exact separation 2 versus 6 and the first lengths at which amplification is possible and maximal are useful for stability and finite-window analyses; they cannot be read off from monotonicity of a single rank statistic.
